Subject: ACME POC — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Liam & Sofia,

Thanks again for the time this morning — great alignment on goals for the POC. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary / success criteria (as discussed):
- Latency: median end-to-end generation latency <= 400ms for 512-token prompts under your expected concurrency (we'll validate with our load script).
- Cost: target $0.006 per 1k tokens or better based on streaming and batching configs.
- Quality: >= 90% on your sample of 200 intent-specific prompts (we'll run evals and share results).
- Integration: minimal code changes — use Redwood SDK + streaming endpoint; support for tool calling is required for external knowledge lookup.

Next steps / ownership:
1) Redwood: share integration checklist and MOA for legal (attached). Owner: me. Due: EOD Wed (2026-06-30).
2) ACME: share engineering point-of-contact and provide placeholder API keys for sandbox. Owner: Liam. Due: Tue (2026-06-30).
3) Technical sync: schedule 60m with ACME eng + Redwood SE to walk integration plan (SDK, streaming, tool calling). Owner: Rachel/Michael. Target dates: Thu-Fri (2026-07-01/02).
4) Validation plan: we'll run a 2-week trial with your sample prompts and report on latency/cost/quality. Owner: joint.

Attachments: redwood-poc-moa.pdf, acme-integration-checklist.xlsx

I'll follow up separately with a detailed integration plan for your engineers. Please reply with the best POC engineer and ideal time windows for the technical sync.

Best,

Subject: Re: ACME POC — technical integration plan (SDK, endpoints, streaming, tool calling)

Hi Sofia / Liam — copying the proposed engineering plan below so you can share with your team. Happy to run the demo during the technical sync.

=== Redwood POC integration plan (high-level) ===
1) SDK & auth:
- Use our official Node/Python SDKs (npm: @redwood/inference, pip: redwood-inference).
- For the POC use-case, install SDK + set REDWOOD_API_KEY (sandbox key we'll provide).
- Example (Node):
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-west-2' });

2) API routes & sample calls:
- Standard generate endpoint for synchronous calls: POST /v1/generate (body: model, prompt, max_tokens, temperature).
- Streaming: ws://stream.redwoodinference.com/v1/stream?model=redwood-rl-1 -> supports chunked tokens and partial JSON for tool call events.
- Tool calling: we support structured tool-calls via our tool schema (see examples). The runtime will emit a tool_call event; your service should listen on the callback URL and return JSON with tool result.

3) Recommended config for ACME workload:
- Model: rwl-2-large-v1 (verified throughput profile for 512-token workloads).
- Quantization: 8-bit; batching: dynamic with 50ms coalescing window for interactive latency.
- Streaming: enabled (reduces perceived latency and cost for your UI flows).

4) SDK example for streaming with tool calling (Node):
- Connect via WebSocket, handle 'token' and 'tool_call' events, and POST results to our tool callback endpoint. We'll provide a short code sample in the shared Drive folder.

5) Security & sandbox:
- Sandbox keys are scoped to the ACME trial and IP-restricted if requested.
- Logging: we can enable verbose per-request tracing to help debug POC issues; production traces are retained per contract.

6) Validation plan & metrics collection:
- We'll run automated load jobs capturing latency by percentiles, token counts, and cost per 1k tokens.
- We'll run your 200-sample quality evals and push results to the shared Drive scoring sheet.

7) Owner assignments:
- ACME eng lead: Sofia Torres (integration dev).
- Redwood SE: Michael Grant (technical lead).
- Redwood AE: Marissa Cole (commercial lead).

If you can confirm Sofia's availability for Thu 7/1 4:00pm ET, I'll schedule the invite and attach the demo plan.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
